newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids raised to $65-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids raised to $65-feedlots.

text.p: Packers raised their bids for Plains-area feedlot cattle by $1 to $65 per cwt on Tuesday but no sales were reported with owners still pricing cattle at $66 and $67, feedlot sources said.
"They have upped their bid to $65 and I think we will see $66 bid in the next 20 to 30 minutes the way they are acting," a Kansas cattle feeder said.
Dealers said though, that it was unclear how many feedlots would accept $66 given that August CME live cattle futures had moved above 68 cents a lb by 1115 CDT.
"It will be a hard decision," the Kansas source said.
The bulk of trade last week was at $64 per cwt.
Strong product values were a supportive factor.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values, as of 1130 CDT, were up $2.38 to $1.56 per cwt.
